response.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT c.location AS city, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) AS race_count FROM circuits c LEFT JOIN races r ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM qualifying q WHERE q.raceId = r.raceId) GROUP BY c.location), shares AS (SELECT city, race_count, race_count * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(race_count) FROM city_counts) AS share FROM city_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT s.city, s.race_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS above_avg_by FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY s.share DESC

assumptions.assumption: A race counts as having qualifying data if at least one qualifying row exists for its raceId; duplicate qualifying rows per race do not inflate the count.
A city is the distinct circuits.location string; circuits with the same location text in different countries are merged into one city.

The average share is the unweighted mean over all distinct circuit cities, including cities with zero qualifying races (share 0). The total is the sum of race counts over those same cities, and each race is counted once because it belongs to one circuit.

alternatives.interpretation: The average share is taken only over cities that have at least one race with qualifying data, so zero-count cities are excluded from the average. The total and shares are unchanged.
alternatives.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT c.location AS city, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) AS race_count FROM circuits c LEFT JOIN races r ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM qualifying q WHERE q.raceId = r.raceId) GROUP BY c.location), shares AS (SELECT city, race_count, race_count * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(race_count) FROM city_counts) AS share FROM city_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares WHERE race_count > 0) SELECT s.city, s.race_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS above_avg_by FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY s.share DESC

alternatives.interpretation: A city is the pair of location and country, so same-named locations in different countries are kept separate.
alternatives.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT c.location || ', ' || c.country AS city, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) AS race_count FROM circuits c LEFT JOIN races r ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM qualifying q WHERE q.raceId = r.raceId) GROUP BY c.location, c.country), shares AS (SELECT city, race_count, race_count * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(race_count) FROM city_counts) AS share FROM city_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT s.city, s.race_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS above_avg_by FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY s.share DESC
